evidence.reason: Appends Entry{Index,Term,Data} to node.log, sets node.commit, then emits append-entries to all peers; this is the external application workload entrypoint.
Peer-to-peer protocol input boundary (message ingress); excluded from external input by the obligation protocol_ingress_excluded.
Logical-time event advancing election/heartbeat elapsed counters; excluded from external input by the obligation timer_and_internal_events_excluded.
Explicitly omits membership changes and snapshots, so Propose is the sole external workload entrypoint; no other business-input API exists.

external_input.boundary: protocol_library: real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary
external_input.reason: Node.Propose(data []byte) is the only workload entrypoint originating outside the protocol: it appends an application entry to the log, advances commit, and emits append-entries to peers. Node.Step is the peer-to-peer protocol ingress and Node.Tick is the logical timer, so both are excluded as required.
limitations: membership_change listed in the protocol brief is not implemented (doc.go: omits membership changes); only Propose is available as external workload input.

evidence.reason: Step is the normal protocol input boundary and is distinct from Propose; it is not treated as external input.

protocol_ingress_excluded.reason: Node.Step (node.go:134) is documented and used as the protocol input boundary; the external workload path Node.Propose is a separate method that never routes through Step.

evidence.reason: Tick advances one unit of logical protocol time; it is an internal timer event, not external input.

timer_and_internal_events_excluded.reason: Node.Tick (node.go:110) is an explicit logical-time event and node.go:80 wall-clock use only seeds the RNG; neither is treated as an external workload entrypoint.

workload_entrypoint.reason: Node.Propose (node.go:148-168) accepts application bytes and writes them into the replicated log, satisfying the requirement to identify input originating outside the protocol as application work.

evidence.reason: Sets running=false; Tick and Step return ErrPaused. Comment at line 170: 'Pause and Resume model a scheduler pause, not process crash/restart.'
Clears running=false; resumes execution without restoring any state, so it is not a recovery boundary.
Comment: 'Node owns both persistent-looking and volatile-looking state in one object. Pause and Resume only control execution; they do not define crash recovery.'
term, vote, log, commit, role, leader, votes all live in one in-memory struct with no durable storage or persistent/volatile split.
Construction always starts from zero state; no load/recover path exists.

lifecycle_control.boundary: protocol_library: durable storage and process crash/restart behavior are outside the boundary; the target itself defines no persistence
lifecycle_control.gap: No restart/recovery boundary exists (Pause/Resume are explicitly not crash recovery), and persistent vs volatile state is not defined or separated.
lifecycle_control.reason: Pause/Resume exist but are explicitly documented as a scheduler pause, not crash recovery (node.go:170), and the Node struct owns all persistent-looking and volatile-looking state in one in-memory object (node.go:46-47) with no recoverable/volatile separation. There is no restart or recovery path and no persistent/volatile semantics. Missing recovery plus missing state-ownership/persistent semantics requires INVASIVE.
limitations: Durable storage is outside the system boundary, but the target provides no persistence hook, so crash-surviving state (term, voted_for, log, snapshot per protocol brief) is never materialized.
lifecycle_control.suggested_direction: Cannot be exposed as recovery without inventing the persistent/volatile split; an Agent would have to decide which state survives a crash, so exposing lifecycle to tests requires invasive changes to state ownership or must be left out of v0.1.

evidence.reason: Documentation states crash recovery is not defined; all state is in-memory only.

persistent_volatile_semantics_defined.reason: The code explicitly states the opposite: 'Pause and Resume only control execution; they do not define crash recovery' (node.go:47) and no persistent/volatile split exists.

evidence.reason: Comment: 'Pause and Resume model a scheduler pause, not process crash/restart.'

restart_or_recovery_boundary.reason: No restart or recovery API exists. Pause/Resume (node.go:171-181) are a scheduler pause explicitly not equivalent to crash/restart, and NewNode always starts from empty state.

evidence.reason: Single struct mixes persistent-looking (term, vote, log, commit) and volatile (role, leader, votes, elapsed) fields.

state_ownership_defined.reason: The Node struct (node.go:48-70) owns all state in one object; recoverable state (term, vote, log) is not separated from volatile state (role, leader, votes, elapsed counters), and no ownership model for recoverable state is defined.

evidence.reason: running=false gates both Tick (ErrPaused at node.go:114) and Step (ErrPaused at node.go:141).

stop_boundary.reason: Pause()/Resume() (node.go:171-181) define an exact stop/pause boundary: running=false makes Tick and Step return ErrPaused (node.go:113, 140), and Resume restores execution. Its meaning is documented as a scheduler pause.

evidence.reason: Single outbound funnel: iterates messages and calls node.transport.Send(message); the only call site of Transport.Send in the package, so it is the point where the original send path can be intercepted and suppressed.
Leader heartbeats and campaign vote requests both reach emit via appendMessagesLocked/campaignLocked; no outbound message bypasses emit.
Inbound processing returns outbound messages that also flow through node.emit, so responses are captured by the same funnel.
Proposal-triggered append entries also flow through emit.
Deep-clones entries so a captured message can be retained in a stable snapshot after Send returns.
The original uncontrollable send path: it synchronously calls target.Step, so a captured message must not continue along this path automatically.

message_capture.boundary: protocol_library: capture applies at the protocol's outbound funnel before the environment-owned Transport.Send path
message_capture.gap: No capture controller exists: NewMessageController(Transport), ListPending() (with ID, From, To, Type, CaptureSequence), and ClearPending() from the testing contract are all absent, and emit currently always forwards to transport.Send without any capture/suppress mode.
message_capture.reason: Every outbound protocol message is created inside stepLocked/campaignLocked/appendMessagesLocked and exits exclusively through Node.emit (node.go:332-340), the single funnel that calls transport.Send. This funnel is a complete suppression point: heartbeats (appendMessagesLocked(nil) from Tick), vote requests, and append entries all pass through it; there are no retries, snapshots, or forwarded requests. Message.Clone (message.go:39) provides stable deep copies. What is missing is purely additive: a NewMessageController(Transport) with ListPending()/ClearPending() and capture-and-suppress semantics in emit, so the change is PATCHABLE, not invasive.
limitations: MemoryTransport.Send delivers synchronously to target.Step; in test mode that delivery must be suppressed at emit. Message identity (ID/CaptureSequence) does not exist yet and must be introduced. Real network send is outside the boundary.
message_capture.suggested_direction: Add a controller seam at Node.emit: when capture mode is enabled, clone the message, assign a CaptureSequence, store it in the pending store, and skip transport.Send. Add NewMessageController(Transport)/ListPending()/ClearPending() as pure additions.

evidence.reason: Normal protocol input boundary; verifies To == node.id and processes the message synchronously under the mutex.
message.Clone() ensures the injected message content is processed unchanged and the caller's copy is never mutated.
Returns ErrPaused when the target is paused; a failed injection (e.g. paused target) can leave the pending message unconsumed.
Message type dispatch handles request_vote, request_vote_response, append_entries, append_entries_response; all legal captured messages are accepted.

message_injection.boundary: protocol_library: injection re-enters the target through the normal protocol input boundary Node.Step
message_injection.gap: Inject(messageID) with consume-on-success / keep-on-failure semantics does not exist, and the required message_id_scope declaration (pending_store_instance or test_session) is not made. Message identity is not yet assigned.
message_injection.reason: The normal protocol input boundary is Node.Step (node.go:134), which selects the target via message.To == node.id (ErrWrongTarget otherwise, node.go:136), processes synchronously under node.mu, and operates on message.Clone() so sender, receiver, and content remain unchanged. An Inject(messageID) operation is a pure addition: look up a pending captured message by ID, call target.Step, and consume it only on success (leave pending on failure, e.g. ErrPaused). Processing is synchronous, so deterministic delivery is achievable. No semantic change to the protocol core is required, hence PATCHABLE.
limitations: Injection is synchronous within Step; outbound messages produced during injection re-enter the capture funnel (outbound capture may occur concurrently per the contract). Real network transport is outside the boundary.
message_injection.suggested_direction: Add a controller method Inject(messageID) that resolves the pending store instance/test session, delivers the recorded message via target.Step, and removes it from the pending set only on nil error.

evidence.reason: Returns role, term, vote, leader, commit index, last log index, and randomized election timeout under node.mu.
LastIndex: uint64(len(node.log)) provides the log range upper bound.
Returns deep-cloned delivered messages, enabling observation of the global message flow.
Resets the delivered log for observation.

observation.boundary: protocol_library: observation covers in-memory node state and transport-recorded messages
observation.reason: Node.Status (node.go:183-197) exposes ID, Running, Role, Term, Vote, Leader, CommitIndex, LastIndex, and RandomizedElectionTimeout under the mutex — covering the protocol-specific minimum (role, term, commit_index, log range via LastIndex). MemoryTransport.Delivered (transport.go:47) exposes stable clones of delivered messages and is already exercised by the tests. No new API is required for v0.1 verification.
limitations: No applied_index exists in this implementation (no apply path), so it is not observable. Full log entry contents are not exposed (only LastIndex); cluster-level state is limited to MemoryTransport.Delivered. Peers are not exposed.

evidence.reason: random is seeded from time.Now().UnixNano() + config.ID with no injection seam; same initial state cannot be reproduced.
Sole consumption of the RNG: randomizedElectionTimeout = electionTick + random.Intn(electionTick); one call site makes a seed/rand injection trivial.

randomness_control.boundary: protocol_library: randomness control targets the RNG used inside the protocol core
randomness_control.gap: No way to fix or inject the random source; a Config.RandomSource/Seed field or equivalent setter is required to make initial state + seed produce repeatable choices.
randomness_control.reason: The only protocol-relevant randomness is the randomized election timeout: NewNode seeds rand.New(rand.NewSource(time.Now().UnixNano()+int64(config.ID))) (node.go:80) and resetElectionTimeoutLocked draws randomizedElectionTimeout = electionTick + random.Intn(electionTick) (node.go:325). The seed is derived from the wall clock and there is no Config field or setter to inject a seed or rand.Source, so choices are not repeatable today. Adding an injectable seed/rand.Source to Config is a contained, single-call-site change: PATCHABLE.
limitations: Wall-clock seeding only affects election-timeout randomness, not protocol time itself.
randomness_control.suggested_direction: Add an optional seed or rand.Source to Config (e.g. Config.RandomSource), used by NewNode when provided, falling back to the current wall-clock default.

evidence.reason: Advances exactly one unit of logical time; increments heartbeatElapsed or electionElapsed and emits heartbeats/campaigns at thresholds.
Only wall-clock use (RNG seed); it does not advance protocol time, so time remains fully tick-driven.
Existing test confirms no state changes without Tick, i.e. time only advances via explicit ticks.

time_control.boundary: protocol_library: time is logical and fully driven by the explicit Tick API
time_control.reason: The accepted v0.1 form 'explicit_tick' is met: Node.Tick (node.go:110) advances exactly one unit of logical protocol time, incrementing heartbeatElapsed (leader) or electionElapsed (follower/candidate) and firing heartbeats or campaigns when thresholds are reached. No protocol timing uses wall clock: the only time.Now() use (node.go:80) seeds the RNG, which belongs to randomness_control. There is no ForceTimeout or ForceElection API. Deterministic advancement of protocol-observed time is therefore supported.
limitations: The exact tick at which an election fires depends on randomizedElectionTimeout, which is drawn from the RNG; repeatable tick counts therefore also require randomness_control (currently PATCHABLE).
